title: Multiplication pulls a symmetric cubical line back to its square-exponent power
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $p:G\to S$ a commutative group scheme with identity $e$, meaning that its addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities. Let $(L,r,\tau)$ be a cubical rigidified line [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. Assume a cubical rigidification-preserving isomorphism $\iota:[-1]^*(L,r,\tau)\simeq(L,r,\tau)$ is given. For every integer $d\geq1$, write $[d]:G\to G$ for the sum of $d$ copies of the identity homomorphism. There is a cubical rigidification-preserving isomorphism $[d]^*(L,r,\tau)\simeq(L,r,\tau)^{\otimes d^2}$. Tensor powers have the tensor product rigidification and cube section, and pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. The assertion imposes no invertibility condition on $d$ on $S$.

source.place: I 5.5, quadratic multiplication formula, used in II 3.3.3. Local original WANTED. Agent specialization of the cubical finite-difference identity to symmetric rigidified lines.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal L=(L,r,\tau)$, $A_j=[j]^*\mathcal L$ for $j\geq0$, and $\mathbf1$ for the trivial cubical line. Tensor products and homomorphism pullbacks are cubical: their defining symmetry, normalization and cocycle equations are obtained by multiplying or pulling back the equations of [def-sfb-cubical-rigidified-line]. The inverse line has the dual rigidification and inverse cube section. The underlying pullback/tensor and composite-pullback identifications are those of [lem-weil-pbc-invertible-pullback-tensor](1),(2). They preserve cube sections because each factor is pulled back along the same composite homomorphism. Cancellation $M\otimes M^{-1}\simeq\mathbf1$ is evaluation: on a local frame it sends $u\otimes u^\vee$ to $1$, and on cube sections it multiplies a section by its inverse. Thus all these operations preserve rigidifications and cubes. The rigidification $r$ identifies $A_0=p^*e^*\mathcal L$ with $\mathbf1$: its cube section is the pullback of $\tau(e,e,e)=1$. Also $A_1\simeq\mathcal L$.

source.place: Base cases and tensor cancellation; extension from field-valued underlying lines to the supplied cubical rigidification.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-cube-section-cubical-compatibility]. For any commutative $S$-group scheme $H$ and homomorphisms $a,b,c:H\to G$, pull its cubical isomorphism back along the homomorphism $(a,b,c):H\to G^3$. Cancel dual factors as in step 1, and use $r$ on the zero-map factor. The result is a cubical rigidification-preserving isomorphism
$$(a+b+c)^*\mathcal L\otimes a^*\mathcal L\otimes b^*\mathcal L\otimes c^*\mathcal L\simeq(a+b)^*\mathcal L\otimes(a+c)^*\mathcal L\otimes(b+c)^*\mathcal L.$$
Denote it by $C(a,b,c)$. It is the actual pulled-back cube section with factors moved across by evaluation. This supplies preservation of cube sections, which the underlying theorem of the cube alone would not supply.

source.place: The cube relation pulled back along three homomorphisms; cubical compatibility isolated in the cited supporting node.

proof.text: Evaluate $C(a,b,c)$ at $H=G$, $a=b=\mathrm{id}_G$, $c=[-1]$. Here $a+b+c=\mathrm{id}_G$, $a+b=[2]$, and $a+c=b+c=0$. Consequently $\mathcal L^{\otimes3}\otimes[-1]^*\mathcal L\simeq A_2\otimes A_0^{\otimes2}$. The cubical symmetry $\iota$ in the hypothesis and the identification of $A_0$ in step 1 give $A_2\simeq\mathcal L^{\otimes4}$. This uses neither division by $2$ nor uniqueness of a rigidification-preserving isomorphism.

source.place: Substitution $(x,x,-x)$, giving the multiplication-by-two base case.

proof.text:
For $n\geq1$ use $C(\mathrm{id}_G,\mathrm{id}_G,[n-1])$ from step 2; it is cubical by [lem-sfb-cube-section-cubical-compatibility]. The seven sum maps give
$$A_{n+1}\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes2}\otimes A_{n-1}\simeq A_2\otimes A_n^{\otimes2}.$$
Prove simultaneously $A_{n-1}\simeq\mathcal L^{\otimes(n-1)^2}$ and $A_n\simeq\mathcal L^{\otimes n^2}$ by induction on $n\geq1$. For $n=1$ these are $A_0\simeq\mathbf1$ and $A_1\simeq\mathcal L$. In the induction step insert these two isomorphisms and the $A_2$ isomorphism of step 3 into the displayed relation. Tensor both sides with the inverse of $\mathcal L^{\otimes(2+(n-1)^2)}$ and evaluate the inverse pairs. This gives
$$A_{n+1}\simeq\mathcal L^{\otimes(4+2n^2-2-(n-1)^2)}=\mathcal L^{\otimes(n+1)^2},$$
since $4+2n^2-2-(n-1)^2=(n+1)^2$. Together with the previous isomorphism for $A_n$ this is the next pair. Each map is a tensor product or composite of cubical rigidification-preserving maps. Taking $n=d$ proves the assertion for every $d\geq1$. Only integer exponent arithmetic was used, so no integer was required to be a unit on $S$.

source.place: Substitution $(x,x,[n-1]x)$ and the explicit simultaneous induction; same finite-difference route as the current blueprint.
